The cliques are completely separate, with no edges between them, so each one is its own community." width="100%"} Creates `num_cliques` complete graphs ("caves") of `clique_size` nodes each and leaves them unconnected. With `L` cliques of `k` nodes, the graph has `L * k` nodes, `L * k(k - 1)/2` edges, and `L` connected components. It is the extreme case of community structure, with every edge inside a community and none between them, and the starting point for the connected and relaxed caveman graphs (see `add_connected_caveman_graph()` and `add_relaxed_caveman_graph()`). Each node's cave (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, so the planted communities can be compared with what a detection method finds. The caves are created one after another, each as a consecutive run of node IDs; in a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Caveman graphs are useful for: - sanity checks for community detection, which should recover the caves exactly - modeling isolated, tightly knit groups (Watts's "caveman world" of small societies) - a baseline against which to compare the relaxed and connected variants ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [num_cliques]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of cliques. Must be at least `1`. [clique_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each clique. Must be at least `1`. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's clique index. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `num_cliques=` or `clique_size=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three caves of four nodes give `12` nodes, `3 * 6 = 18` edges, and three separate components: ::: {#7d281f43 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_caveman_graph(num_cliques=3, clique_size=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), graph.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (12, 18, 3) ``` ::: ::: The `community` attribute holds the cave of each node. Since no edge leaves a cave, this partition reaches `1 - 1/3`, the highest modularity any split into three groups can score: ::: {#b54c1a19 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.modularity("community") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.6666666666666666 ``` ::: :::
